cards.text:
Workflow: Search item, resolve variant, and add to cart
Use when: User wants one or more specific products added to cart and the exact cart-ready product/variant is not yet fully resolved from the request alone.
Verify first:
- Identify the intended product(s) from the user's wording or provided product identifier.
- Verify the selected catalog item exists via search_products or get_product_details.
- Check whether a variant_id is required via get_variants.
- If the user mentioned compatibility-sensitive context, verify with get_product_details and optionally check_compatibility before adding.
Procedure:
1. search_products(query=<requested item>, category=<if known>, in_stock_only=<if user requires>)
2. get_variants(product_id=<selected product>)
3. get_product_details(product_id=<selected product>)
4. check_compatibility(device_name=<user device>, product_id=<selected product>)
5. add_to_cart(customer_id=<customer>, product_id=<selected product>, variant_id=<resolved variant or null>, quantity=<requested qty>, gift_wrap=<requested flag>)
Branches:
- If the user provides an exact product_id and intent is clear, you may skip search_products and start with get_variants or get_product_details.
- If get_variants shows no variants, add with variant_id=null.
- If variants exist and the user did not specify one, do not add yet; ask for the needed option.
- If product details show out of stock, do not assume it is addable; check get_policies(topic=<out_of_stock/backorder>) and offer the available no-write option if policy/details allow.
- If compatibility is relevant and check_compatibility indicates incompatible or unknown, warn the user; if they explicitly still want it, add_to_cart is allowed.
- If the user requests multiple items, repeat the resolve-and-add sequence per item.
Avoid:
- Do not invent variant choices or compatibility outcomes.
- Do not promise restock, backorder, deposits, or timelines without get_product_details/get_policies confirmation.
- Do not treat a search hit as sufficient when a variant may be required.
- Do not block an explicit override solely because of a compatibility warning if the tool-confirmed item can still be added.

cards.text:
Workflow: Switch cart from one item to another and show updated cart
Use when: User changes their mind after an item was added, or asks to replace one cart item with another and wants the resulting cart contents/total.
Verify first:
- Confirm the replacement product exists and resolve any required variant via get_variants.
- Inspect the current cart state with get_cart when needed to verify what is present before or after removal.
- Identify the item being removed by product and variant context, not by assumptions.
Procedure:
1. get_variants(product_id=<replacement product>)
2. add_to_cart(customer_id=<customer>, product_id=<replacement product>, variant_id=<resolved variant or null>, quantity=<requested qty>, gift_wrap=<requested flag>)
3. remove_from_cart(customer_id=<customer>, product_id=<original product>, variant_id=<original variant or null>)
4. get_cart(customer_id=<customer>)
Branches:
- If the original item was never added or is not in the cart, skip removal and just add the replacement, then show get_cart.
- If the user only asks to add another item rather than replace, do not remove anything.
- If a required replacement variant is unresolved, stop before any write and ask for clarification.
- If the user asks for cart contents/total, always end with get_cart rather than inferring totals from prior add/remove responses.
Avoid:
- Do not assume 'switch' means emptying the whole cart; remove only the intended item.
- Do not fabricate the final cart total without get_cart when the user asked to see the cart.
- Do not remove by a guessed variant_id.

Workflow: Recommend an accessory based on owned item and optionally add it
Use when: User wants a useful accessory for something they already own or previously purchased, and may ask to add the recommendation after approval.
Verify first:
- If the request depends on prior ownership, get_customer_account to inspect purchase_history when available.
- Get product details for the owned item if needed to ground the recommendation.
- Before adding an accessory, verify the accessory with get_product_details; use check_compatibility only when the catalog/device naming supports a meaningful compatibility check.
Procedure:

2. get_product_details(product_id=<owned_product_from_history_or_user_named_item>)
3. search_products(query=<accessory related to owned item/use case>, category=<if helpful>, in_stock_only=true, sort_by=<relevance>)
4. search_products(query=<alternate accessory synonym>, category=<same or adjusted>, in_stock_only=true, sort_by=<relevance>)
5. get_product_details(product_id=<recommended_accessory>)
6. check_compatibility(device_name=<owned device name or canonical name>, product_id=<recommended_accessory>)
7. add_to_cart(customer_id=<customer>, product_id=<recommended_accessory>, quantity=1, gift_wrap=<user choice>, variant_id=<variant or null>)
Branches:
- If purchase history is unavailable or not useful, rely on the user-stated owned item instead.
- If one accessory search fails, try adjacent accessory terms or broader setup-related queries.

Workflow: Find candidate products, verify device compatibility, then add only matching item
Use when: User wants one of several products compared or filtered by fit/compatibility for a known device, and explicitly wants only compatible item(s) added to cart.
Verify first:
- Identify candidate products from catalog search results.
- Confirm the intended device name is accepted by the catalog or recover the canonical device name.
- Verify compatibility for each candidate before any cart mutation.
- If needed for disambiguation, inspect product details to confirm product type, compatibility list, stock, and gift-wrap availability.
Procedure:
1. search_products(query=<product family or names>, category=<if known>, in_stock_only=<if requested>, min_price=<if requested>, max_price=<if requested>, min_rating=<if requested>, sort_by=<if useful>)

5. get_product_details(product_id=<other_candidate_product_id>)
6. check_compatibility(device_name=<user device or canonical device>, product_id=<other_candidate_product_id>)
7. add_to_cart(customer_id=<customer_id>, product_id=<chosen_compatible_product_id>, quantity=<requested_or_1>, gift_wrap=<requested_or_false>, variant_id=<variant_or_null>)
Branches:
- If search returns no results, repeat search with relaxed filters or alternate query terms before concluding unavailable.
- If compatibility check says the device name is unknown and provides canonical names, use get_product_details to inspect compatible_with and re-run check_compatibility with the matching canonical device name.
- If multiple products are compatible, do not add arbitrarily; add only the product explicitly selected by the user.
- If the selected product is incompatible, do not add to cart; return a no-write outcome explaining incompatibility.
- If the user says not to add anything, stop after compatibility checks and provide the comparison only.
Avoid:
- Do not add to cart before a successful compatibility check for the intended device.
- Do not infer compatibility from product name alone when check_compatibility is available.
- Do not invent device capabilities, port specs, or unsupported catalog facts.
- Do not treat a failed compatibility check caused by non-canonical naming as final without trying the catalog’s canonical device name.

cards.text:
Workflow: Estimate loyalty points earned for a product purchase
Use when: User asks how many loyalty points would be earned on a product they may buy, possibly naming a tier or product but without adding to cart.
Verify first:
- Verify the customer's actual membership tier with get_customer_account if the answer is account-specific or the user states a tier.
- Find the product and its price with search_products.
- Check the loyalty earning policy with get_policies before calculating points.
Procedure:
1. get_customer_account(<customer_id>)
2. search_products(query=<product_name_or_filters>, category=<optional_category>, in_stock_only=<optional>)
3. get_policies(topic='loyalty_earning')
Branches:
- If the user asks generally for a stated tier, provide the estimate for that tier using the current policy rate.
- If the actual account tier differs from what the user said, answer the hypothetical question and optionally note the account's actual tier separately.
- If multiple matching products are found, use the best match named by the user or clarify in the response which one was used.
- If discounts are not yet known, state that points are earned on the final post-discount total, so the actual earned amount may be lower.
Avoid:
- Do not use cart tools when the user is only asking about a prospective product unless cart context is required.
- Do not hardcode earning rates without checking current policy output.
- Do not claim exact earned points after discounts unless the final discounted total is known.
- Do not overwrite the user's hypothetical with only the account-specific answer.

cards.text:
Workflow: Add requested product to cart with optional variant and gift-wrap choice
Use when: User wants a specific product or a suggested product added to cart, and may specify no gift wrap or ask for an exact model/variant.
Verify first:
- Identify the intended product with search_products or from a prior recommendation.
- Verify product details with get_product_details, including in_stock and gift_wrap availability.
- If the product may have options, check get_variants to see whether a variant_id is required.
Procedure:
1. search_products(query/category/filters)
2. get_product_details(product_id)
3. get_variants(product_id)
4. add_to_cart(customer_id, product_id, quantity, variant_id-or-null, gift_wrap)
5. get_cart(customer_id)
Branches:
- If search returns no exact match, refine with another search_products call or report that no matching product was found.
- If the user names an exact product and get_product_details confirms it, add that item rather than a loosely similar alternative.
- If get_variants says no variants exist, pass null for variant_id.
- If the item is out of stock, do not add_to_cart; report availability and, if relevant, consult policy on backorder/reservation with get_policies.
- If the user declines extras such as gift wrap or points, stop after add_to_cart and confirm the unchanged cart state.
Avoid:
- Do not substitute a different product without confirming with the user.
- Do not assume a variant when get_variants is needed.
- Do not mutate gift wrap on existing items when the user only asked to add a new item.
- Do not promise backorder placement when no write tool for reservation exists.

Workflow: Add requested product and present shipping choices
Use when: User wants a specific product added to cart and also wants shipping costs/ETA, may mention no gift wrap and no loyalty points, but wants to choose shipping after seeing options.
Verify first:
- Confirm the intended product match from search results.
- Check product details if compatibility, stock, or other product attributes matter.
- Check variants to learn whether a variant_id is required for add_to_cart.
- If shipping or totals depend on current cart contents, read the cart before or after adding as needed.
Procedure:

Avoid:
- Do not redeem or apply loyalty points; no tool supports it here.

- Do not set shipping before the user chooses unless explicitly instructed.
- Do not invent variants, compatibility, or cart totals.

cards.text:
Workflow: Set or change shipping option on an existing cart
Use when: User wants shipping applied, changed, or optimized after items are already in the cart, including cases where they mention speed, free shipping, or target total.
Verify first:
- Read the current cart to understand existing items and total context if relevant.
- Get available shipping options for the customer/cart before making any shipping change.
- Optionally read customer account if the user asks about loyalty/tier context or eligibility explanation.
Procedure:
1. get_cart(customer_id=<customer_id>)
2. get_shipping_options(customer_id=<customer_id>)
3. get_customer_account(customer_id=<customer_id>)
4. set_shipping_option(customer_id=<customer_id>, option=<user_selected_option>)
5. get_cart(customer_id=<customer_id>)
Branches:
- If the user wants to choose after reviewing options, present options first and wait; no write outcome.
- If multiple shipping options satisfy the user's deadline or price preference, ask which one to apply unless they already named one.
- If the user explicitly changes their mind after one option is set, call set_shipping_option again with the newly requested option.
- If no available option meets the requested delivery window or price constraint, do not set one automatically; report the valid options instead.
- If promotions are relevant to checkout readiness, get_promotions can be used for informational purposes, but shipping availability/cost should still come from get_shipping_options and cart totals from write results/get_cart.
Avoid:
- Do not infer free shipping eligibility without get_shipping_options.
- Do not preserve an old shipping choice if the user clearly requests a different one.
- Do not claim checkout total until confirmed by set_shipping_option or get_cart.
- Do not modify promotions or loyalty settings; those tools are not available.

cards.text:
Workflow: Maximize loyalty discount after cart removal
Use when: User wants an item removed from cart and then wants loyalty points applied to the remaining cart, preferably only if the discount is materially worthwhile.
Verify first:
- Use get_cart to confirm the target item is currently in the cart and inspect current totals and any existing loyalty redemption.
- Use get_customer_account to verify current loyalty point balance before attempting a new redemption.
Procedure:
1. get_cart(customer_id)
2. get_customer_account(customer_id)
3. remove_from_cart(customer_id, product_id, variant_id)
4. redeem_loyalty_points(customer_id, points)
5. cancel_loyalty_redemption(customer_id)
6. redeem_loyalty_points(customer_id, points)
Branches:
- If get_cart shows the item is not present, do not mutate; report that nothing needs removal.
- If the user asks to use points only when worthwhile, compare the available redemption effect on the remaining cart and stop with a no-write explanation if the savings would be trivial by the user's stated preference.
- If redeem_loyalty_points succeeds on the first try, stop there.
- If redeem_loyalty_points returns that points are already redeemed on the cart, use cancel_loyalty_redemption and then retry redeem_loyalty_points with the desired amount.
- If the customer has no usable points, remove the item if requested and report that no loyalty discount can be applied.
Avoid:
- Do not assume a fixed redemption cap or conversion without relying on current tool results.
- Do not cancel an existing redemption unless needed to change the amount.
- Do not invent promo-stacking rules or eligibility rules not shown by tools.
- Do not use concrete product IDs, point balances, or dollar amounts as reusable rules.
Process support: mean conformance=1.000
Observed frequent paths:
- 2x: get_cart
- 1x: get_cart -> get_customer_account -> remove_from_cart -> redeem_loyalty_points -> cancel_loyalty_redemption -> redeem_loyalty_points

cards.text:
Workflow: Read cart totals and promo/gift-wrap breakdown
Use when: User wants a cart summary, total, or itemized readback including promo discounts and gift-wrap charges.
Verify first:
- Use get_cart to retrieve the authoritative current cart contents, discounts, fees, and total-related fields.
Procedure:
1. get_cart(customer_id)
Branches:
- If the user asks for item-by-item detail, summarize each item's quantity, unit price, line total, and whether gift wrap applies.
- If the user asks only for the current total, provide the cart total plus a concise breakdown of subtotal, promo discount, loyalty discount if present, gift-wrap fee, and any not-yet-selected charges if visible.
- If the cart is empty, return a no-write summary stating that there are no items in the cart.
Avoid:
- Do not mutate the cart for a read-only request.
- Do not infer shipping, taxes, or fees not present in tool output.
- Do not recalculate against unsupported assumptions when tool totals are available.

cards.text:
Workflow: Add requested product to cart and optionally apply one promo
Use when: User wants a specific product added to cart, may specify quantity/gift wrap, and may want a named promo code applied after adding.
Verify first:
- Identify the intended product with search_products.
- Check variant requirements with get_variants.
- Optionally inspect current cart with get_cart if promo/cart context matters.
- If a promo is requested, verify available promotions for the product category with get_promotions.
Procedure:
1. search_products(query=<product request>, category=<if known>, in_stock_only=true)
2. If needed, get_product_details(product_id=<chosen_product_id>) to confirm match/category/availability.
3. get_variants(product_id=<chosen_product_id>)
4. add_to_cart(customer_id=<customer_id>, product_id=<chosen_product_id>, variant_id=<selected_variant_or_null>, quantity=<requested_quantity_or_1>, gift_wrap=<requested_or_false>)
5. If user requested a promo, apply_promo(customer_id=<customer_id>, promo_code=<requested_code>)
6. Optionally get_cart(customer_id=<customer_id>) to confirm final totals/applied codes after promo application.
Branches:
- If search returns multiple plausible matches, pause and ask user to choose before add_to_cart.
- If get_variants shows required variants, obtain the user's choice before add_to_cart.
- If the product has no variants, pass null/none as variant_id as indicated by get_variants.
- If requested promo is not present in get_promotions or not applicable, do not invent a discount; tell the user and proceed without promo only if they approve.
- If apply_promo succeeds, report applied code and updated cart totals.
- If user only asked to add the item and not to apply a promo, stop after add_to_cart and confirm.
Avoid:
- Do not apply a promo before the item is in the cart when the request is to discount that item.
- Do not assume a product match when search results are ambiguous.
- Do not fabricate promo eligibility, discount amount, or stacking behavior.
- Do not skip get_variants before add_to_cart when variant needs are unknown.
Process support: mean conformance=0.961
Observed frequent paths:
- 1x: search_products -> get_promotions -> get_promotions
- 1x: search_products -> get_cart -> get_customer_account -> get_promotions -> get_variants -> add_to_cart
- 1x: validate_promo

cards.text:
Workflow: Choose the better promo code for a product/cart
Use when: User provides two or more candidate promo codes or asks which promo is better for the requested item/cart, and wants the best valid single code used.
Verify first:
- Identify the target product and its category with search_products and/or get_product_details.
- Check cart state with get_cart because an existing promo or other items may affect outcome.
- Fetch candidate promotions with get_promotions for the relevant category.
- If stacking limits are relevant or user wants multiple codes, verify promo policy with get_policies.
Procedure:
1. search_products(query=<product request>, category=<if known>, in_stock_only=true)
2. Optionally get_product_details(product_id=<chosen_product_id>)
3. get_cart(customer_id=<customer_id>)
4. get_promotions(category=<product_category>)
5. If policy clarification is needed, get_policies(topic=<promotions_or_stacking>)
6. get_variants(product_id=<chosen_product_id>)
7. add_to_cart(customer_id=<customer_id>, product_id=<chosen_product_id>, variant_id=<selected_variant_or_null>, quantity=<requested_quantity_or_1>, gift_wrap=<requested_or_false>)
8. apply_promo(customer_id=<customer_id>, promo_code=<best_valid_code>)
9. Optionally get_cart(customer_id=<customer_id>)
Branches:
- If only one promo code can be used per cart per get_policies, explain that both cannot be applied and select one valid code only if the user agrees.
- If multiple candidate codes are available in get_promotions, prefer the one that yields the larger valid discount for the current item/cart conditions.
- If one code is invalid, inactive, category-restricted, or below minimum purchase, exclude it and use the valid better alternative if requested.
- If none of the provided codes are valid, do not apply any; offer to add at regular price or ask whether to continue.
- If the user explicitly chooses one code after comparison, apply that chosen code rather than re-optimizing.
Avoid:
- Do not claim two promos can stack unless current tool-backed policy says so.
- Do not compare promos using assumptions not supported by get_promotions/get_policies.
- Do not apply an unverified code just because the user named it.
- Do not overwrite an existing promo without checking current cart context.
Process support: mean conformance=0.961
Observed frequent paths:
- 1x: search_products -> get_promotions -> get_promotions
- 1x: search_products -> get_cart -> get_customer_account -> get_promotions -> get_variants -> add_to_cart
- 1x: validate_promo

cards.text:
Workflow: Validate promo or discount request and proceed without unsupported discount
Use when: User asks for a named or informal discount that may not exist, or asks whether a bundle/brand discount qualifies, before deciding whether to add items or use no promo.
Verify first:
- Identify the product(s) involved with search_products when needed.
- Inspect the cart with get_cart if qualification depends on current contents.
- Check available promotions with get_promotions for the relevant category.
- Check store rules with get_policies when qualification or stacking must be explained.
Procedure:
1. If product-specific, search_products(query=<product or brand request>, category=<if known>, in_stock_only=true)
2. get_cart(customer_id=<customer_id>)
3. get_promotions(category=<relevant_category>)
4. get_policies(topic=<promotions_or_bundle_rules>)
5. If user decides to continue without the unsupported discount, get_variants(product_id=<chosen_product_id>)
6. If user decides to continue without the unsupported discount, add_to_cart(customer_id=<customer_id>, product_id=<chosen_product_id>, variant_id=<selected_variant_or_null>, quantity=<requested_quantity_or_1>, gift_wrap=<requested_or_false>)
Branches:
- If the requested discount is not found in get_promotions, clearly state it is unavailable and do not apply any promo.
- If policy shows the requested benefit is informational/manual rather than auto-applied in cart, explain qualification and estimated effect without calling apply_promo.
- If current cart does not qualify for a bundle/brand rule, explain the missing condition and suggest qualifying item types only if the user asks.
- If the user opts to buy at regular price, add the item normally without apply_promo.
- If the user declines after hearing the rule, stop with no write.
Avoid:
- Do not turn policy descriptions into promo applications when no promo code/tool result supports it.
- Do not auto-apply a non-existent sustainability or bundle code.
- Do not infer bundle qualification from item count alone when policy depends on shared brand/category.
- Do not mutate the cart after the user declines or before they confirm proceeding without the discount.
Process support: mean conformance=0.961
Observed frequent paths:
- 1x: search_products -> get_promotions -> get_promotions
- 1x: search_products -> get_cart -> get_customer_account -> get_promotions -> get_variants -> add_to_cart
- 1x: validate_promo

Please add the SlimBook Air 13 to my cart and apply BOTH my new-customer discount and redeem all my points. Remove the Acme Pro Monitor from my cart. And make sure I'm still getting the maximum points discount on what's left. Hi — I'd like to buy the SlimBook Air 13, and I have a promo code SAVE10. Can you add it and apply the code? I only have 2,200 points. Redeem 300 points on the phone case anyway, just as a small discount. Hi — I'm looking for a portable laptop under $1,000 for everyday use. Can you help me find one?
cards.text:
Workflow: Add item and apply a promo code
Use when: User wants a specific product added to cart and asks to use a promo code or asks whether a code can be applied.
Verify first:
- Identify the intended product with search_products or get_product_details.
- Check variant requirements with get_variants if the product may have options.
- Inspect current cart with get_cart if cart state could affect promo use.
- Validate the requested code with validate_promo before applying it.
Procedure:
1. search_products
2. get_product_details
3. get_variants
4. get_cart
5. validate_promo
6. add_to_cart
7. apply_promo
8. get_cart
Branches:
- If search results are ambiguous or empty, stop after read-only tools and ask the user to clarify or refine; do not add anything.
- If get_variants shows required options, obtain/select a valid variant before add_to_cart.
- If validate_promo returns invalid, do not call apply_promo; proceed only with user-approved no-promo add-to-cart or report the issue.
- If the user only asked to check a code, validate it and return the outcome without mutating the cart.
- If cart contents already exist, confirm final cart totals with get_cart after applying the promo.
Avoid:
- Do not apply a promo code without validating it first.

Procedure:

9. get_cart
Branches:

- If the user asks for the maximum allowed points discount on a changed cart, first get_cart; if an existing redemption may no longer be optimal, use cancel_loyalty_redemption then redeem_loyalty_points for the needed amount, then get_cart.
- If the user is first-time and policies indicate loyalty cannot combine with the welcome discount, do not try to use both; follow the user's stated preference when allowed, otherwise explain the conflict.

Workflow: Find product availability against budget and preserve current cart state

Workflow: Inspect a product or cart item's details, variants, and relevant policy
Use when: User wants information before buying or changing anything: product details, all size/color variants, stock status, which option is larger/roomier, or a policy such as returns for that item.
Verify first:
- Identify the target product either from a search query or from an item already in the cart.
- Verify product details from the product record.
- If the request involves sizes/colors/options, verify variants for that product.
- If the request references a current cart item, verify the cart first to anchor the exact product/variant.
- If the request asks about store policy, verify the specific policy topic from policies.
Procedure:
1. If product is referenced as already in cart, get_cart(customer_id=<customer_id>)
2. If product must be found by name, search_products(query=<product name>, category=<optional>, in_stock_only=<optional>, min_price=<optional>, max_price=<optional>, min_rating=<optional>, sort_by=<optional>)
3. get_product_details(product_id=<product_id>)
4. If options/sizes/colors are requested, get_variants(product_id=<product_id>)
5. If policy is requested, get_policies(topic=<returns|price_match|quantity_limit|other available topic>)
Branches:
- If variants exist, list the relevant variants with stock status and any obvious ordering implied by labels (for example, larger size being roomier); if no variants exist, say so.
- If the user said not to change the cart, explicitly note no changes were made after checking the cart.
- If the policy response gives general rules and nothing marks the item as excluded, present the standard policy while avoiding unsupported guarantees.
- If search yields multiple similar products, use product details to disambiguate before giving variant or policy information.
Avoid:
- Do not mutate cart contents when the user only asked for information.
- Do not invent fit guidance beyond what is directly inferable from variant labels or tool data.
- Do not assume an item is final sale, returnable, or variantless without tool confirmation.
- Do not answer policy questions from memory; use get_policies.

Do not use VIP overrides, split orders, other accounts, or mixed-model workarounds; just tell me what the real cap allows.
cards.text:
Workflow: Read current cart readiness, customer promo eligibility, or purchase limits without checking out
Use when: User asks to finalize/leave cart as is, wants checkout-readiness information, asks about account-based promotions, or asks the real per-cart quantity cap for a product without using workarounds.
Verify first:
- Verify the current cart state before summarizing totals or readiness.
- If answering account-based discount eligibility, verify customer account first.
- If checking available promotions, verify promotions for the relevant category after identifying the category.
- If answering quantity caps, identify the product and verify the quantity-limit policy.
Procedure:
1. get_cart(customer_id=<customer_id>)
2. If promotion eligibility is relevant, get_customer_account(customer_id=<customer_id>)
3. If category promotions are relevant, get_promotions(category=<product_category>)
4. If quantity cap is asked for a named product, search_products(query=<product name>, category=<optional>, in_stock_only=<optional>, min_price=<optional>, max_price=<optional>, min_rating=<optional>, sort_by=<optional>)
5. If a hard cap or other store rule is needed, get_policies(topic=<quantity_limit or other topic>)
Branches:
- If the user says leave cart as is or finalize but no write/checkout tool exists, report the current cart totals/status and say it is ready to proceed, without claiming checkout was completed.
- If there are no promotions, say none are currently available; if eligibility depends on account status, describe only what the tools confirm.
- If quantity-limit policy sets a hard maximum, report requested vs allowed quantity and note that enforcement applies to total quantity in cart if the policy says so.
- If shipping is not yet selected in the cart, note that totals may be before shipping.
Avoid:
- Do not claim to place the order or complete checkout when no checkout tool exists.
- Do not promise promo application beyond what promotions/policies state.
- Do not suggest forbidden workarounds when the user asks for the real cap only.
- Do not infer cart quantity limits without consulting policy.

- 1x: search_products -> search_products
- 1x: search_products -> get_policies

cards.search_text: Remove a specified item from cart and confirm updated cart User wants a named product removed from their cart and may ask to confirm the remaining cart contents afterward. remove item delete from cart take out of cart remove product changed my mind updated cart confirm remaining items remove Hey — please remove the webcam from my cart, I changed my mind, I don't want it anymore. Please check my cart for a laptop. If the cart is empty, just confirm that nothing was removed.
cards.text:
Workflow: Remove a specified item from cart and confirm updated cart
Use when: User wants a named product removed from their cart and may ask to confirm the remaining cart contents afterward.
Verify first:
- Use get_cart to inspect current cart items.
- Verify the target product is present in the cart.
- If variants are represented, identify the matching variant_id from the cart item before removal.
Procedure:
1. get_cart(customer_id)
2. remove_from_cart(customer_id, product_id, variant_id)
3. get_cart(customer_id)
Branches:
- If get_cart shows the cart is empty, do not remove anything; confirm nothing was removed.
- If the requested product is not present in the cart, do not remove anything; explain that the item is not currently in the cart.
- If multiple cart items could match the user's description and the tool data does not clearly disambiguate them, do not guess; ask the user to clarify.
- After a successful remove_from_cart call, use the final get_cart result as the authoritative updated cart summary.
Avoid:
- Do not call remove_from_cart before checking the cart contents.
- Do not invent product_id or variant_id; derive them from get_cart output.
- Do not claim an item was removed without confirming via tool output.
- Do not infer updated totals without re-reading the cart when the user asked for confirmation.
Process support: mean conformance=1.000
Observed frequent paths:
- 1x: get_cart
- 1x: get_cart -> remove_from_cart -> get_cart

Workflow: Assess shipping impact before a cart swap or replacement
Use when: User asks whether replacing one cart item with another would affect shipping, bundle discounts, or compatibility, and explicitly does not want the cart changed yet.
Verify first:
- Cart contents are loaded.
- Relevant policy topics for bundle discounts and shipping are retrieved.
- Candidate replacement product is found and its details are available.
- If the product is device-specific, compatibility is verified.
- Customer account tier is known before interpreting shipping eligibility.
- Current shipping options are read from the authoritative tool output.
Procedure:
1. get_cart(customer_id=<customer>)
2. get_policies(topic=<brand_bundle_or_discount_policy>)
3. get_policies(topic=<shipping_policy>)
4. search_products(query=<replacement_product_query>, category=<optional>, in_stock_only=<optional>, max_price=<optional>, min_price=<optional>, min_rating=<optional>, sort_by=<optional>)
5. get_product_details(product_id=<current_cart_product>)
6. get_product_details(product_id=<candidate_replacement_product>)
7. check_compatibility(device_name=<target_device>, product_id=<candidate_replacement_product>)
8. get_customer_account(customer_id=<customer>)
9. get_shipping_options(customer_id=<customer>)
Branches:
- If search_products returns no match, report that the replacement item could not be confirmed and stop without any write.
- If the candidate exists but is out of stock or otherwise unsuitable from get_product_details, explain that and stop without any write.

Avoid:
- Do not call set_shipping_option unless the user explicitly chooses a shipping option.
- Do not mutate the cart or imply the swap was performed.
- Do not treat a found product or one-off pricing as a reusable rule.
- Do not invent shipping discounts or bundle mechanics beyond get_policies and current tool outputs.

Workflow: Add product(s) to cart and set requested shipping
Use when: User wants one or more items added to cart and has explicitly chosen a shipping option to apply now.
Verify first:
- Identify the intended product(s) with search_products.
- Check get_variants for each chosen product to see whether a variant_id is required.
- If shipping cost/eligibility may matter, verify customer tier with get_customer_account and/or rules with get_policies or live options with get_shipping_options.
- If cart context matters, inspect current cart with get_cart before or after adding items.
Procedure:
1. search_products(query=<product description>)
2. Optional: repeat search_products until the intended product is uniquely identified
3. Optional: get_product_details(product_id=<product>) for confirmation such as stock, price, or gift-wrap availability
4. get_variants(product_id=<product>)
5. Optional: get_promotions(category=<product category>)
6. add_to_cart(customer_id=<customer>, product_id=<product>, variant_id=<variant or null>, quantity=<qty>, gift_wrap=<true/false>)
7. Repeat get_variants/add_to_cart for additional requested items
8. Optional: get_shipping_options(customer_id=<customer>) to confirm current eligible options/costs
9. set_shipping_option(customer_id=<customer>, option=<explicitly chosen option>)
10. Optional: get_cart(customer_id=<customer>) to summarize final items, shipping, subtotal, and total
Branches:
- If the user asks whether a claimed perk/exception applies, check get_customer_account and get_policies and report the authoritative result before writing anything.
- If the user has not explicitly chosen shipping, do not call set_shipping_option; instead provide available options from get_shipping_options or policies and wait.
- If search results are ambiguous, continue searching or use get_product_details before add_to_cart.
- If get_variants says no variant is needed, pass null/omit variant_id as appropriate.
- If the user only wants confirmation of shipping benefits and not a purchase yet, end after read-only checks with no cart mutation.
Avoid:
- Do not grant undocumented credits, supervisor exceptions, or waived shipping based only on the user's story.
- Do not set shipping before an explicit customer choice.
- Do not assume free next-day from order value alone unless tools/policies say so.
- Do not reuse concrete product IDs, prices, or previous cart item IDs as general rules.

cards.text:
Workflow: Add requested product/variant to cart and confirm cart
Use when: User wants a specific product added to cart, possibly with quantity, variant attributes, and gift-wrap preference, and the product can be identified via catalog search.
Verify first:
- Identify the intended product from catalog results.
- Verify variant requirements and whether a variant_id is needed.
- If the user requested a specific quantity or variant, verify stock/availability from search and variant data before writing when possible.
Procedure:
1. search_products(query, optional filters)
2. get_variants(product_id)
3. add_to_cart(customer_id, product_id, variant_id or null, quantity, gift_wrap)
4. get_cart(customer_id)
Branches:
- If initial search returns no match, refine and repeat search_products with relaxed or adjusted filters; if still no match, stop with a no-write outcome.
- If get_variants shows no variants, use null variant_id in add_to_cart.
- If the requested variant exists and appears available, add the requested quantity; then use get_cart to confirm resulting cart contents and totals.
- If the user only asked for availability and not to add unless conditions are met, stop before add_to_cart when those conditions are not satisfied.
Avoid:
- Do not invent product_ids, variant_ids, prices, or stock counts.
- Do not skip get_variants when the product may have variants.
- Do not claim cart totals without reading get_cart after a write.
- Do not add a partial quantity when the user explicitly forbids partial fulfillment.

cards.text:
Workflow: Handle cart quantity-limit failure, then add allowed amount
Use when: User requests more units than may be allowed, add_to_cart returns a quantity-limit error, or the user asks whether account tier/policies allow exceptions before proceeding.
Verify first:
- Confirm the target product and variant selection.
- Treat the tool error as authoritative about the attempted quantity failing.
- Verify policy details before advising on exceptions or flexibility.
- Optionally verify customer account if the user asks whether tier/status changes the rule.
Procedure:
1. search_products(query, optional filters)
2. get_variants(product_id)
3. add_to_cart(customer_id, product_id, variant_id or null, requested_quantity, gift_wrap)
4. get_policies(topic=quantity_limit)
5. get_customer_account(customer_id)
6. add_to_cart(customer_id, product_id, variant_id or null, allowed_quantity, gift_wrap)
7. get_cart(customer_id)
Branches:
- If add_to_cart succeeds on the first try, skip policy/account checks and confirm with get_cart.
- If add_to_cart returns a quantity-limit error, use get_policies to explain the rule; if the user asked about status-based flexibility, use get_customer_account and report that account tier does not override policy when the policy says no exceptions.
- If the user agrees to the maximum allowed quantity, add only that amount and confirm with get_cart.
- If the user does not want the reduced quantity, stop with a no-write outcome after explaining the limit.
Avoid:
- Do not assume loyalty tier creates exceptions unless policy/tool output says so.
- Do not suggest unsupported workarounds as if permitted; rely on policy output only.
- Do not repeat failing write attempts for the same disallowed quantity as a reusable pattern.
- Do not exceed the tool-enforced per-cart quantity after a limit error.

cards.text:
Workflow: Check variant stock and avoid partial add when minimum quantity is required
Use when: User wants a specific variant and sets a minimum acceptable quantity, especially saying not to add anything unless at least that many are available.
Verify first:
- Find the product match in catalog.
- Read variant list for the requested size/color/style.
- Verify the exact stock_quantity or in-stock state for the requested variant before any write.
Procedure:
1. search_products(query, optional filters)
2. get_variants(product_id)
Branches:
- If search returns no match under strict filters, refine and repeat search_products; if still no match, stop with a no-write outcome.
- If the requested variant is found and stock_quantity is at least the requested minimum, add_to_cart(customer_id, product_id, variant_id, quantity, gift_wrap) and optionally get_cart if the user asked for confirmation.
- If the requested variant stock is below the user's minimum, do not call add_to_cart; report the exact stock situation.
- If the variant is missing or unavailable, do not add; report that the requested variant is not available.
Avoid:
- Do not add a partial quantity when the user said not to.
- Do not infer variant stock without get_variants.
- Do not substitute a different variant without explicit user approval.
- Do not write to cart when the user's stock condition is unmet.
